lens: detection power: which observed invariants separate honest from tampered/inconsistent logs most sharply, with the lowest measured honest false-positive rate and the smallest detectable deviation

proposals.name: Server-minted id bracket and binding test (provider request/response ids as a third clock bound to each response)
proposals.observation_summary: ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O5 (skeptic numbers): one constant client-server skew per stream places every server-id time between the stream's last input event and the response's first output block in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat streams (rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466]; tolerance 0 gives 18, 5 s gives 7); cc_local 1 of 847; aiv_cu Anthropic opus/sonnet/haiku/fable 105/80/27/32 and Gemini pro/flash 255/92 streams all 0; OpenAI 3/463. Skew-interval width U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms. Placebo on 3,673 swechat streams: rolling the id sequence by one response flags 3,667; moving one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441, 30 s earlier flags 3,581; moving it 5 s, 30 s or 300 s later flags 10, which equals the baseline. ids/O1: swechat request ids are v7|var2 in 154,815/154,815 against 2,418.98 expected by chance; cc_local 31,085/31,085. ids/O2: counting every copy, request-id time agrees with the client stamp in 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992]; holdout A 11,047 ids, 0 violations. ids/O6: a naive offset >= 0 rule fails on client skew (cc_local 125 violations in 3 sessions, min -7,749 ms) that the bracket absorbs. ids/O7: in 2 re-stamped session pairs the id clock picks the earlier copy in 178/178 (disagreeing offsets >= 619,473 ms vs agreeing 2,347-21,734 ms).
proposals.test_measurement: Extend the O5 placebo scripts (scratchpad rd/o5.py, o5b.py, o5c.py) into a tamper suite on swechat B Claude Code streams, holding the honest rate at 10/3,674 and reporting session-clustered CIs: (1) insert a fabricated tool_result before response k, stamped on a grid of offsets (0.5-60 s) before and after the request-id time; (2) splice a whole response with its request id from another session, or from later in the same session; (3) delete one response; (4) back-date one response on a 1-30 s grid (finer than the measured 5 s / 30 s points) to locate the displacement giving power 0.5 and 0.9, to be compared with U-L p50 2,268 ms; (5) collapse a block of entries onto one timestamp as in ids/O7. Replicate on holdout A (11,047 ids), cc_local (847 streams) and aiv_cu Anthropic (post-switch), Gemini and OpenAI streams. Report power per tamper type, not pooled.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 10/3,674 swechat streams inconsistent at 2 s tolerance (18 at 0 s, 7 at 5 s); client clock skew behind the server (ids/O6: cc_local min -7,749 ms, split A -16,359 ms), which breaks per-event rules but leaves the bracket at 1/847; resume/fork copies with re-stamped history (ids/O7: 2 session pairs, 477 entries), which is why counting every copy lowers O2 agreement to 0.99871 with 190 offsets over 10 min; second-resolution ids (ids/O3: OpenAI and Gemini ids have 1 s resolution; aiv_cu OpenAI 3/463 inconsistent).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent cannot see or predict the id: the provider mints it when the request arrives (ids/O2 mechanical explanation), so a model fabricating results in-band cannot produce a consistent one. A log editor can: the ids are unsigned base58/hex strings and anyone who knows the layout (itself UNVERIFIED against documentation, ids/O1) can mint a v7 id with a chosen time for an inserted or moved response. Late-stamping is invisible by construction (later shifts flag only the baseline 10), resolution is per turn rather than per event, and edits that leave timing alone (content substitution, status flips) are invisible.
proposals.coverage: Measured where server ids exist: swechat 155,267 (session, request) ids in 1,638 sessions forming 3,674 streams; cc_local 31,085 request ids, 847 streams; aiv_cu Anthropic only after the 2026-07-06 message-id switch (ids/O4: 0 UUIDv7 msg ids from 2025-04 to 2026-06), Gemini 255/92 and OpenAI 463 streams. aiv_cc has none (ids/O13: 0 request ids stored). Share of all tool results constrained: not measured; a stream needs at least 2 responses.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake) is a known general technique. Using LLM-provider request ids as a per-stream skew bracket and a response-binding test on agent tool logs may not be described; we have not checked. It is neither a capture-side witness (the id already exists) nor a hash chain.
proposals.rank_reason: The only invariant with a measured tamper-power curve: misbinding is flagged in 3,667 of 3,673 streams and a 30 s back-date in 3,581, against an honest 10 of 3,674, using a value the agent cannot see.

proposals.name: Visible-text vs harness structured-copy recount at 1-unit resolution
proposals.observation_summary: raw_census/A6-O1 (skeptic, full population): Claude Code's harness Read counter toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the number of line-numbered lines in the model-visible result text in 87827/88229 = 0.9954, Wilson [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960] over 4603 files. All 402 mismatches are named harness or dataset formats: 282 persisted-output previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 '<identical to result [rN]...>' references, 7 redacted contents and 1 negative line numbers; none is unexplained. cc_local main 570/578, all 8 mismatches empty-file warnings with diff -1. raw_census/A6-O2: a subagent's totalToolUseCount equals its distinct nested tool_use ids in 6623/6623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], 1934 files. raw_census/A6-O4: the same structured copy also carries Edit structuredPatch line counts (70553/73460 = 0.960 filled) and Grep numLines (29535/34208 = 0.863); their agreement with the visible text was not measured.
proposals.test_measurement: Pre-register the whitelist from A6-O1 (persisted-output preview, offset warning, identical-to reference, REDACTED, negative line numbers; plus cc_local's empty-file warning) and re-run on the full swechat CC population and cc_local main; the expected honest unexplained count is 0. Tamper suite on a random sample of clean Read results: add or delete 1, 2 or 5 lines; splice in a same-path Read result from another session; substitute content with the line count held fixed. Report detection per tamper type; arithmetic predicts every line-count change is caught and no count-preserving substitution is, and the run should confirm both. Do the same for A6-O2 by deleting or inserting one nested tool_use in agent_progress traffic. Then measure agreement, not only presence, for Grep numLines vs result lines and for Edit structuredPatch oldLines/newLines vs the call's old_string/new_string line counts, and report their honest unexplained rates.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: the 402 swechat mismatches are all harness display formats or dataset redaction, and cc_local's 8 are empty-file warnings (diff -1); a detector without the whitelist would fire on every one. Not false positives but blind spots: 2150/8773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] of Agent/Task results have no nested traffic and cannot be checked (A6-O2); cc_local subagent files carry no Read numLines (0 of 12); Glob totalMatches is absent in swechat (0/6422).
proposals.evasion_cost: Low for a schema-aware editor. Both fields are written by the same harness from the same read (A6-O1 and A6-O2 mechanical explanations: internal redundancy, not an independent witness), so rewriting numLines alongside the text evades the check, and line-count-preserving substitutions are invisible by construction. The model does not author toolUseResult, so a model writing a fake result into its own text produces no counter at all. The check therefore targets post-hoc edits made without schema knowledge and harness or export faults, not in-band claims.
proposals.coverage: Read results carrying numLines: 88229/90763 = 0.972 in swechat (A6-O4); cc_local main 578/650 = 0.889. Agent/Task results checkable: 6623 in 1934 files, with 2150/8773 uncheckable. Edit and Grep counters are present (0.960, 0.863) but their agreement is not yet measured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Consistency between redundant fields is a generic data-integrity idea. Using Claude Code's toolUseResult structured copy as a cross-check on the model-visible result seems unexplored to us, but we have not checked. It differs from Tool Receipts (purpose-built, capture-side) because the field already exists, and it is neither recomputation of the command (METR) nor output grammar parsing (jc).
proposals.rank_reason: Among the lowest measured honest false-positive rates in the data, and the only one of them tied to result content (0 unexplained in 88229 Read results once 5 named formats are whitelisted; 6623/6623 subagent counts), at 1-line or 1-call resolution; ranked below rank 1 because both fields come from one writer.

proposals.name: Execution-window consistency: time evidence in or around a result must fit the window in which it was supposedly produced
proposals.observation_summary: Nearly every fresh clock reading or timer we checked that real execution leaves in or around a result fits that result's own call-to-result window, and most exceptions have a cause visible in the log (re-reads, display rounding, re-stamped blocks). commit_witness/O9 (skeptic): commit SHAs printed in Bash results resolve for 3936 claims in 1491 sessions, and commit_date lies in [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s] for 3917 = 0.995 [0.992, 0.998], median offset -0.103 s. commit_witness/O11: of the 19 claims whose commit_date precedes the window, 15 are cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files, 1 is an amend with an explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE and 3 are unexplained. ext_witness/O10: epochs printed with a fractional part (time.time() form) never postdate the external wiki save, 0/459 (Wilson upper 0.0083); without a fraction 7/123. two_clocks/O6: Codex's model-visible 'Wall time' header never exceeds the call-to-output gap for exec_command (0 violations in 4408 at 2 ms, min slack 153 ms), while 0.1 s-display shell_command headers exceed it in 646/1817 by <= 49 ms. two_clocks/O8: harness tool timers lie inside the window (swechat Glob 1/2090, WebFetch 0/341, WebSearch 0/158, Task 0/1023, Agent 0/1886), and two_clocks/O12 places that one Glob case on a timestamp shared by 180 entries. two_clocks/O9: bash_progress ticks obey the floor rule in 0/112677 violations (Wilson hi 3.41e-5, 687 sessions), result >= last tick 5676/5676, per-call phase residual range median 6 ms. Negative control ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O14: stored v7 uuids printed in results are not fresh (440 of 561 mentions more than 10 min older), so only freshly generated readings qualify.
proposals.test_measurement: On swechat CC B raw transcripts and Codex rollouts: (1) classify each result's printing command as generator or re-reader using a list fixed in advance from commit_witness/O11 (cat/tail/head/grep of a file, TaskOutput and background .output reads are re-readers); (2) extract fresh absolute readings (resolved git '[branch sha]' to commit_date; ISO datetimes and 10-digit epochs from generator commands) and printed durations (Codex 'Wall time', test-runner 'in X s', shell 'real'); (3) compute the honest violation rate per class with session-clustered CIs, with tolerance 2 s for absolute readings (from O9) and the printed resolution for durations (from O6); (4) for swechat sessions that emit bash_progress, measure the share of Bash calls with gap >= 3 s that carry at least one tick, and tick count vs gap (not yet measured); (5) tamper suite: replay a real clock-bearing output from earlier in the session or from another session for the same command, shift stamps by a grid of deltas, drop ticks; report power vs delta at the measured honest rate. Stop rule: if fresh readings occur in too few results to matter, report that share and stop.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: re-reads of saved output (15 of the 19 out-of-window commit claims, identifiable by command); explicit committer dates (1); 3 unexplained of 3936 resolved claims; display rounding (shell_command headers 646/1817, by <= 49 ms) and write_stdin poll stamps (14/1600, min -36.1 ms); bulk re-stamped blocks (two_clocks/O12; timing checks must abstain on tie runs); machine suspend (two_clocks/O10: 1 progress event over its timeout among 83521); stored ids and dates echoed by tools (ids/O14); auto-backgrounded commands whose result window is not the execution window (outliers/O9: 111 of 188 swechat 120 s shell results were auto-backgrounded); sandbox clock offset (ext_witness/O10 median -1 s). A SHA that does not resolve is not usable alone: 2198/6141 = 0.358 [0.321, 0.394] of honest commit claims do not resolve (commit_witness/O10).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent sees neither the harness stamps nor future commit dates at second resolution, so it cannot print a consistent fresh reading without actually running a command. A log editor controls the stamps, so for plain date-style outputs and Wall time headers they can keep printed values and stamps in step once they know the rule. The git leg costs more: the commit date is hashed into the SHA and the commit lives in an external repo, so moving a commit claim in time, or inventing one, needs a real commit made at that time. Forging ticks needs a phase-locked 1 Hz chain whose first tick falls at elapsed 2 or 3 s.
proposals.coverage: Measured pieces only: resolved commit claims 3936 in 1491 sessions (out of 6141 claims in 1839 sessions); Codex exec_command Wall time headers 4408; bash_progress ticks on 5702 calls (687 sessions) in swechat, none in cc_local (raw_census/A6-O10: no progress entries); fraction-form epochs 459, in collusion-wiki only. Share of all tool results that carry a fresh clock or a printed duration: not measured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Unlike METR-style recomputation of deterministic outputs (echo, wc), this bounds outputs that cannot be recomputed by the log's own clock. Timestamp-consistency auditing is generic, and the git leg overlaps our own git shadow-state plan.
proposals.rank_reason: Second-scale resolution with rare honest misses that the printing command mostly explains (19 of 3936 commit claims, 15 of them re-reads), partly anchored on a content-addressed external object; ranked third because the share of results carrying a fresh clock is unmeasured.

proposals.name: Quantized server-usage ledger of result modality (per-image and cache-block units)
proposals.observation_summary: token_conservation/TC9 (skeptic): in aiv_cu Gemini the per-window change in prompt IMAGE tokens is 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11668 of 11668 pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro, n 4925; 1064 for 3-pro 682, 3.1-pro 3166 and 3.5-flash 2895), never negative. It is positive in 5059/5092 GUI windows and 0 in every non-GUI window: shell 0/4134, get_pixel_coords 0/2033, pause 0/202. distributions/D3: prompt-side image tokens sit on the per-model lattice in flash 3219/3219 and pro 10569/10569 ({258, 1064, 2160}), and no session mixes lattices (0/309). aiv_accounting/O11: in aiv_cc, where screenshots are stripped from the log, the context residual per image is tightly concentrated (pre-registered fit: median 890.1 [887.9-890.9], p25 879.1, p75 892.7, n=4543 pairs in 64 runs), above the honest per-turn |residual| p99 of 690.2 (aiv_accounting/O10). The level depends on the model: a no-intercept model gives 1112.5, and token_conservation/TC17 gives 1035.0 (p5-p95 1016-1142) for aiv_cc but 535.0 (p5-p95 121-1618) for user-pasted swechat images. swechat_tables/T11: Codex cached_input_tokens is a multiple of 128 in 16106/16106 calls.
proposals.test_measurement: aiv_cu Gemini (11945 pairs): predict IMAGE units per window from the logged action types and require dIMAGE = units x per-model constant; measured honest exceptions are 33/5092 GUI windows with no increment and 0 in non-GUI windows. Tamper suite: delete one GUI result, relabel a GUI action as shell, insert a fabricated screenshot-returning call and result, splice in a window from another session; report detection at the honest rate for each direction. Also test the regime above 40 images that the B sample never reached (442 population sessions with more than 40 GUI turns). aiv_cc: count [IMAGE_REMOVED] markers per window, test the residual against the per-image constant, and tamper by adding or removing one marker; report power at FPR 1% with run-clustered CIs, treated as a one-agent case study. Codex: cached_input_tokens % 128 == 0 as a plausibility check on fabricated usage rows.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5092 GUI windows show no increment (not cap effects; images before median 4, max 31); the unit depends on model generation (258, 1064, and 2160 in 70 rows from 3 sessions); cached IMAGE counts are off-lattice (11/3022 and 40/9318), so only prompt-side counts are checkable; aiv_cc has 30 unlogged context resets, 27 of them image pairs (aiv_accounting/O12); user-pasted images vary in size (swechat p5-p95 121-1618), so a per-image constant holds only for uniform screenshots; Claude cache tokens show no 128 granularity (1/563).
proposals.evasion_cost: The model never sees usage metadata. A log editor can rewrite it, since it is unsigned. Screenshots stay in context (up to 40 observed), so adding or removing one image shifts IMAGE and promptTokenCount for every later response in the session, and the editor must propagate the change consistently through all of them. Swapping one screenshot for another of the same unit, or editing text, is invisible to this ledger.
proposals.coverage: Exact ledger only in aiv_cu Gemini: 11945 pairs; two_clocks/O7 puts Gemini rows in 347 of 2000 B sessions. aiv_cc: 4543 single-image pairs in 64 runs of effectively one agent (token_conservation/TC2: all its sessions are runs of a single sdk_session_id). Codex 128 rule: 16106 calls. No per-modality breakdown was observed for Anthropic or OpenAI-chat usage.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Plausibility checks on token counts are familiar in billing. We have not seen the provider's per-modality token counts used as an exact ledger of how many image-returning results a log may contain, but we have not checked.
proposals.rank_reason: Exact, server-written integer witness at 1-image resolution with 0 honest increments across 4134 shell, 2033 get_pixel_coords and 202 pause windows; ranked fourth for narrow coverage (aiv_cu Gemini, plus one-agent aiv_cc).

proposals.name: Frozen usage-ledger reconciliation at tolerance 0 (commit-time tally and end-of-run result row)
proposals.observation_summary: swechat_tables/T1 (skeptic): a 5-integer token/API tally written by the Entire CLI at commit time equals, with tolerance 0, an exact recount of the stored transcript (distinct message.id, last-occurrence usage) over the whole transcript, a prefix or a contiguous window in 4794/4836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions (repo-clustered [0.9874, 0.9942], 183 repos). Prefix sessions are snapshots taken while the session continued: created_at precedes the last transcript timestamp in 1664/1664 prefix sessions, with a median of 3 messages past the snapshot. T2: the window class is explained by the declared checkpoint_transcript_start in 357/357. T3: after correcting a dataset join artifact, unmatched is 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] across 4 scaffolds; Claude format 4822/4836. T4: residual rate by CLI version 0.4.x 11/3691 = 0.0030, 0.5.x 15/1048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235]. aiv_accounting/O7: in Agent SDK runs, result.usage is never above the sum of logged per-response usage (0 of 211 runs); the 15 runs below it are explained exactly by subset sums of responses with non-null stop_reason (12/12, plus 3 all-zero runs). aiv_accounting/O4: num_turns == user rows + 1 in 153/154 non-trivial runs.
proposals.test_measurement: On the swechat sessions with tallies (5701): run a tamper suite on honest sessions inside the snapshotted range. Delete one assistant message (all records of one message.id); insert a message.id copied from elsewhere; append messages after the snapshot point; insert a fabricated tool_use block into an existing message.id; edit result content. Report the detection rate per tamper against the honest unmatched rate 33/5701, overall and per CLI version. The recount rule predicts that 1-message deletions and insertions inside the snapshot are caught, while post-snapshot appends and block-level insertions into an existing message are not; the run should confirm both. Then couple the frozen usage with per-call token conservation and report the smallest content edit detectable once usage cannot be edited; the current per-call figure is swechat CC power 0.5/0.9 at 8913/10000 inserted chars, and 0.0099 at +3000 chars (token_conservation/TC2). Repeat on aiv_cc result rows (211 runs) by deleting or inserting a response with null stop_reason.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5701 unexplained after the join correction, higher in CLI 0.5.x (15/1048) and concentrated by repo (6 of 33 in hirakiuc/gh-orbit); 7 Claude residuals differ only in output_tokens (mid-stream snapshot, T4). The dataset join artifact (T3) must be corrected first, because it accounts for 31 of 64 raw mismatches. Checkpoint rows are duplicated across forks (T9: 3650/13406 rows), which double-counts in repo-clustered statistics. aiv_cc: 15/211 runs fall below the ledger, all explained by non-null stop_reason responses whose omission depends on SDK version and date (O7).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent sees neither ledger. The Entire tally is written at commit time into the entire/checkpoints git branch (T9 mechanical explanation: forks copy that branch), so an editor must rewrite that branch as well; a rewrite is possible but is visible to anyone holding an older clone. Blind spots by construction: anything after the snapshot point; a tool_use block inserted into an existing message.id, since the recount keys on distinct message.id with last-occurrence usage; and any change to tool-result content, since usage does not change when a result is edited (T1 skeptic). Content edits then face only per-call token conservation, which misses edits under thousands of chars (TC2) and never catches deletion of results under 1k chars (TC16: [100,1000) power 0.003). The aiv_cc result row sits in the same log, so an editor can rewrite it together with the stream (aiv_accounting/O5: tokens and cost can be edited together).
proposals.coverage: swechat: tallies for 5701 sessions across 4 scaffolds (Claude format 4836 with api > 0), present only where the Entire CLI ran. aiv_cc: 211 runs of effectively one agent. Every assistant message before the snapshot point is constrained; tool-result content is not.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. The commit-time tally behaves like a seal, and sealing is prior art (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric); ledger reconciliation is a standard audit idea. What may be new is that the seal already exists incidentally (Entire CLI) and freezes the provider usage that token conservation is then checked against.
proposals.rank_reason: Tolerance-0 equality at 1-API-message resolution with an honest unexplained rate of 33/5701 and an anchor stored outside the transcript, but blind to result content and to block-level insertion, so it constrains which turns exist rather than what results said.
